outcomes: One contributor offering distributes canonical skills and worker profiles; publication, language evaluation, load sampling and tree verification use native Go CLI commands
Contributor workflows reach tasks, proposals and memory through the providers the workspace binds, so a backend changes without a skill edit
A repository states its labels, states, workflow profiles, language rule and publication defaults once, in its own configuration
Only build, spec, design, review and check remain as workflow entries, alongside the configured explicit-only content-bump utility; legacy aliases and duplicated orchestration are removed
Build coordinates a requested intention, multi-task issue or epic from observable delivery units through its mandated stage, making demonstrated results, blockers and next actions visible
Material specs, designs, prototypes, ADRs and delivery boundaries receive independent challenge before adoption, with original findings and supported resolutions preserved
Versioned local records carry exact native artifact, handoff and producer references across sessions without creating another requirement registry or controller
nonGoals: Choosing a tasks, proposals or memory provider for the workspace, or falling back to another one
Authorizing publication, merge or deployment: the mandate and the repository's controls still decide
Changing host permissions, credentials or model access, which stay with the workspace and the host
Changing the separately owned audit workflow; its active language relay delegates to the shared native evaluator
Migrating other workspaces' separate agentArtifacts declarations and pins

requirements.text: One @putnami/contributor extension ships build, spec, design, review and check, the explicit content-bump utility, three worker profiles (fix-standard, fix-heavy and reviewer) and shared references for both hosts. Build owns one loop and continues until the requested outcome, concrete blocker or mandate boundary. A workspace opts in with extension:@putnami/contributor.

The configured content-bump utility is explicit-only on both hosts. Canonical workflows remain implicitly available for the requested objective. Implicit selection grants no backlog processing, task mutation, Git publication, merge or deployment authority; local implementation checkpoints remain within the authorized work.

Only canonical workflow entries and active configured utilities are materialized. Removed plan, execute, fix, epic, code-review, fix-loop, adr, prototype and putnami-* entries and the fix-light and epic-analyst workers have no metadata, resource directories or duplicate implementations. Unchanged owned legacy files are removed during upgrade; edited files remain protected and their collision is explicit.

No shipped file invokes a backend client, names a tracker label, a hosted repository address, a private memory identity or storage layout, or this repository's identity. Skills reach tasks, proposals and memory through putnami tasks, proposals or memory operations.
Instructions name worker profiles, never models; a worker profile's host metadata supplies its model, and a workflow profile may name another one for the stage it runs in a separate agent.

When an outcome changes a feature declaration, spec, specs baseline, architecture manifest, decisions file or ADR, build commits those declarations alone and pushes them to its draft before any code. It goes on without waiting, reads reviews and comments before each later checkpoint and before ready, answers a comment on a declaration on the proposal, and gives a declaration changed after its approval its own commit. A change with no declaration keeps the milestone order.

putnami change finalize, launched by the core and served by the @putnami/contributor executable, exits, prints, pushes and writes the same proposal and task records as goldens recorded from putnami proposals finalize, the core command it replaced, for a draft seed, a hosted gate and a usage error.

Both hosts install canonical source/package content with exact resource links, one build recipe index, repeat-install idempotence and edited-file protection. Legacy workflows and shell implementations are deleted; the active audit language relay only calls the native evaluator. Workflow records require advertised native support. Stage changes, reviews, adapters and publication rechecks never execute another gate; actual released adoption is distinct.

Build runs the loop talk, declare, show, code, check, prove, validate, merge from a core under 2,000 tokens and one reference per stage, read only at that stage. It reports each stage with putnami agent stage and sizes its plan with putnami change estimate before code. Code starts without the owner unless the plan spans several slices with important design or spec decisions or touches a sensitive zone; the owner then approves the study and a cost envelope first.

A workflow profile in the contributor policy states, for each loop stage and for review, whether it runs in the main session or in a separate agent, and the worker profile, model and effort of that agent. --profile, then the task label the policy names, selects it, else the default profile, which runs only review in a separate agent. The tier labels and tier workers are gone.

A fresh reviewer agent reviews the frozen candidate. P1 and P2 findings block, P3 findings are listed in the proposal, and a contradiction with an ADR blocks. The main session fixes, a fresh reviewer checks only the P1 and P2 fixes, and after two rounds a disagreement goes to the owner with both positions.
